events.title: Anne Becomes Queen
events.description: On the death of William III, Anne succeeded to the thrones of England, Scotland and Ireland. She was the last Stuart monarch.
events.significance: Her reign saw the 1707 Acts of Union, which joined England and Scotland into the Kingdom of Great Britain.

events.title: The February Revolution Begins in Petrograd
events.description: On March 8 in the modern calendar (February 23 in the Russian calendar then in use), International Women's Day demonstrations in Petrograd grew into strikes and mass protests. These marked the start of the Russian Revolution.
events.significance: Within days the unrest brought down Tsar Nicholas II and ended centuries of Romanov rule. It set the stage for the Bolshevik takeover later that year.

events.title: U.S. Combat Troops Land in Vietnam
events.description: About 3,500 U.S. Marines came ashore at Da Nang, South Vietnam. They were officially there to protect the nearby air base.
events.significance: They were the first major U.S. ground combat unit sent to Vietnam. Their arrival marked a major escalation of American involvement in the war.

events.title: Philips Demonstrates the Compact Disc
events.description: In Eindhoven, the Dutch company Philips showed the international press its prototype Compact Disc audio player. It used digital optical recording.
events.significance: The demonstration was an early step toward the CD. Developed with Sony, the format changed how people bought and listened to music.
